claim: KDM2B is distributed throughout the nucleus and excluded from nucleoli.
source: In contrast to previous reports, we observe that KDM2B is distributed throughout the nucleus and excluded from nucleoli (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Recombinant KDM2B binds non-methylated DNA in vitro.
source: In agreement with previous work, recombinant KDM2B was found to bind non-methylated DNA in vitro (Koyama-Nasu et al., 2007; Yamagishi et al., 2008; Blackledge et al., 2012) in a manner that is comparable to that of KDM2A (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data in Figure 1A,B and cited previous studies

claim: KDM2B binding to non-methylated DNA is abrogated by CpG methylation.
source: Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) demonstrating that the recombinant KDM2B ZF-CxxC domain binds to a DNA probe containing non-methylated CpGs (left panel) in a concentration-dependent manner. Binding is abrogated by CpG methylation (right panel).
evidence: Demonstrated by EMSA data in Figure 1A

claim: Both KDM2A and KDM2B localize to promoter associated CGIs and are excluded from non-CGI associated promoters.
source: A visual inspection of these profiles suggests that both KDM2A and KDM2B localize to promoter associated CGIs and are excluded from non-CGI associated promoters (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq profiles shown in Figure 1C

claim: KDM2A and KDM2B are specifically enriched at CGI associated transcription start sites.
source: When KDM2A and KDM2B ChIP-seq signal was plotted over all transcription start sites (TSSs) that had been segregated based on their classification as CGI or non-CGI associated there was a very specific enrichment of both KDM2A and KDM2B at the CGI associated class of transcription start site (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: KDM2A and KDM2B signal peaks at the centre of CGIs.
source: Furthermore, when KDM2A and KDM2B signal was plotted over all CGIs, including those away from gene promoters, there was a very specific spatial localization of both proteins at CGIs with signal intensity peaking at the centre of the island (Figure 1E).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 1E

claim: KDM2A and KDM2B are both bound to CGIs genome-wide in vivo.
source: Together these observations demonstrate in vivo that KDM2A and B are both bound to CGIs genome-wide.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 1

claim: A subset of CGIs are preferentially enriched for KDM2B and depleted of KDM2A.
source: However when the levels of KDM2A and B were directly compared at individual CGIs genome-wide, a subset of CGIs was found that were preferentially enriched for KDM2B and depleted of KDM2A (Figure 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated by MA-like plot in Figure 2A

claim: Genes associated with KDM2B enriched CGIs are significantly associated with GO terms related to embryo development, morphogenesis, and cellular differentiation.
source: Interestingly, these genes were significantly associated with GO terms related to embryo development, morphogenesis, and cellular differentiation.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2B

claim: Genes involved in early development and embryonic stem cells are often targeted by polycomb repressive complexes.
source: In early development and embryonic stem cells, these classes of genes are often targeted by the polycomb repressive complexes and maintained in a poised but silent state until their expression is induced during lineage commitment (Lee et al., 2006; Boyer et al., 2006; Bracken et al., 2006; Mikkelsen et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited studies

claim: KDM2B is enriched and KDM2A depleted at polycomb occupied CGIs marked by RING1B and EZH2.
source: A heat map illustrating ChIP-seq signal at all CGI transcription start sites (TSSs) in mouse ESC cells indicating depletion of KDM2A and enrichment of KDM2B at polycomb target CGIs marked by RING1B and EZH2.
evidence: Demonstrated by heat map analysis in Figure 2C

claim: The profile of PRC1/2 components over CGI-associated target genes tracks with KDM2B binding and underlying non-methylated DNA signal.
source: Perhaps more surprisingly, the profile of the PRC1/2 components over CGI-associated target genes did not map precisely to the gene TSS but instead tracked with KDM2B binding and the underlying non-methylated DNA signal at these same regions.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-seq profiles shown in Figure 2C-E

claim: There is a spatial relationship between polycomb repressive proteins, KDM2B, and non-methylated DNA.
source: Furthermore, the clear spatial relationship between polycomb repressive proteins, KDM2B, and non-methylated DNA indicates there may be a mechanistic relationship between recognition of non-methylated DNA at CGIs and polycomb repressive complex nucleation.
evidence: Inferred from spatial correlation observed in ChIP-seq data

claim: KDM2B associates with RING1B, YAF2, RYBP, PCGF1, BCOR, and BCORL1 in ESC nuclear extracts.
source: In the purifications from extracts containing epitope-tagged KDM2B a series of proteins in addition to KDM2B were identified (Figure 3B,C). These included RING1B, YAF2, RYBP, PCGF1, BCOR, and BCORL1.
evidence: Demonstrated by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 3B,C

claim: RING1B is the E3 ubiquitin ligase that functions as the catalytic core of the PRC1 complex and is responsible for mono-ubiquitylation of H2A at position 119.
source: Importantly RING1B is the E3 ubiquitin ligase that functions as the catalytic core of the PRC1 complex and is responsible for mono-ubiquitylation of H2A at position 119 (H2AK119ub1).
evidence: Established knowledge about RING1B function

claim: Endogenous KDM2B interacts with RING1B in ESC nuclear extract.
source: To verify that endogenous KDM2B interacts with RING1B, KDM2B was immunoprecipitated from ESC nuclear extract and the presence of RING1B in the immunoprecipitates verified by western blotting (Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 3D

claim: KDM2B exists as part of a variant PRC1 complex in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: Therefore, KDM2B exists as part of a variant PRC1 complex in mouse embryonic stem cells.
evidence: Inferred from protein complex purification and mass spectrometry data

claim: PCGF1 is unique to the KDM2B-PRC1 complex.
source: In the KDM2B purification the only PCGF identified was PCGF1, suggesting that this factor is unique to the KDM2B-PRC1 variant complex.
evidence: Demonstrated by mass spectrometry analysis of KDM2B purification

claim: The PCGF1-containing complex associates with RYBP or YAF2 but fails to integrate chromobox domain-containing (CBX) proteins.
source: Interestingly, in agreement with PRC1 purifications from cancer cell lines (Gao et al., 2012), the PCGF1-containing complex associates with RYBP or YAF2 but fails to integrate chromobox domain-containing (CBX) proteins that recognize H3K27me3 (Cao et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2004a).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data and cited studies

claim: KDM2B forms a PRC1 variant complex that includes BCOR, BCORL1, PCGF1, RING1, and YAF2 or RYBP.
source: Therefore, based on our detailed reciprocal complex purifications, KDM2B forms a PRC1 variant complex that includes BCOR, BCORL1, PCGF1, RING1, and YAF2 or RYBP (Figure 3F).
evidence: Demonstrated by reciprocal affinity purifications and mass spectrometry

claim: An intact PRC1 complex is not required to target KDM2B to polycomb repressed sites in vivo.
source: We then analysed the levels of KDM2B at a series of polycomb repressed and non-polycomb repressed CGI associated genes by ChIP and observed only small or no changes in KDM2B binding in the absence of RING1A/B (Figure 4C). This suggests that an intact PRC1 complex is not required to target KDM2B to polycomb repressed sites in vivo.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP analysis in RING1A/B deleted cells shown in Figure 4C

claim: The ZF-CxxC domain of KDM2B is required for KDM2B binding to CGIs regardless of their polycomb status.
source: ChIP analysis in ESC cells stably expressing tagged wild-type (WT) KDM2B or a mutant KDM2B that disrupts its DNA-binding capacity (K643A).The ZF-CxxC domain of KDM2B is required for KDM2B binding to CGIs regardless of their polycomb status.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP analysis of wild-type and mutant KDM2B shown in Figure 4D

claim: KDM2B localization to regular and polycomb repressed CGIs requires the recognition of non-methylated DNA via the ZF-CxxC domain.
source: This demonstrates that although KDM2B is part of a PRC1 complex its localisation to regular and polycomb repressed CGIs requires the recognition of non-methylated DNA via the ZF-CxxC domain.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP analysis of ZF-CxxC mutant KDM2B

claim: Depletion of KDM2B results in approximately 80% reduction at the RNA level.
source: Knockdown was approximately by 80% at the RNA level (Figure 5A) and there was a clear reduction of KDM2B at the protein level (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-PCR and western blot in Figure 5A,B

claim: Depletion of KDM2B does not result in destabilization of either the PRC1 or PRC2 complexes.
source: Importantly, depletion of KMD2B did not result in destabilization of either the PRC1 or PRC2 complexes allowing us to specifically examine defects resulting from reduced KDM2B (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis in Figure 5B

claim: In KDM2B depletion, 653 genes changed expression by more than 1.5-fold: 329 had reduced gene expression and 324 had increased gene expression.
source: In total 653 genes changed expression by more than 1.5-fold: 329 had reduced gene expression and 324 had increased gene expression.
evidence: Determined by microarray gene expression profiling

claim: 24% of genes up-regulated in KDM2B depletion are characterized by RING1B occupancy.
source: Interestingly 24% of these genes are characterized by RING1B occupancy. This is significantly greater than would be expected by chance (1.9-fold enrichment, hypergeometric p=1.3 × 10−8) and is similar to the percentage of up-regulated genes in the RING1B null ESC cells that are PRC1 targets (Leeb et al., 2010).
evidence: Demonstrated by statistical analysis of microarray and ChIP-seq data

claim: RING1B occupied genes have a clear propensity to have increased gene expression when KDM2B is depleted.
source: Furthermore, when all gene expression changes are depicted in a volcano plot there is a clear propensity for RING1B occupied genes to have increased gene expression when KDM2B is depleted (Figure 5C).
evidence: Demonstrated by volcano plot analysis in Figure 5C

claim: Depletion of KDM2B leads to up regulation of a subset of polycomb repressed target genes in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: Together these findings indicate that as with the removal of RING1B, depletion of KDM2B leads to up regulation of a subset of polycomb repressed target genes in mouse embryonic stem cells.
evidence: Supported by microarray and RT-PCR validation data

claim: 68% of newly identified RING1B binding sites overlap with CGIs.
source: Interestingly, 68% of the 15,740 newly identified RING1B binding sites overlapped with CGIs, and 77% of these were coupled to transcription start sites.
evidence: Determined by ChIP-seq analysis

claim: Clear RING1B peaks are detectable at nearly 70% of the 22,849 mouse CGIs genome-wide.
source: Including the already characterized RING1B associated CGIs, this means that clear RING1B peaks are detectable at nearly 70% of the 22,849 mouse CGIs genome-wide (Illingworth et al., 2010), and 88% of RING1B occupied CGIs also are bound by detectable levels of KDM2B.
evidence: Determined by ChIP-seq analysis

claim: 88% of RING1B occupied CGIs are bound by detectable levels of KDM2B.
source: Including the already characterized RING1B associated CGIs, this means that clear RING1B peaks are detectable at nearly 70% of the 22,849 mouse CGIs genome-wide (Illingworth et al., 2010), and 88% of RING1B occupied CGIs also are bound by detectable levels of KDM2B.
evidence: Determined by ChIP-seq analysis

claim: Depletion of KDM2B causes a specific reduction in RING1B signal at previously identified RING1B CGI associated target sites.
source: To examine whether KDM2B is required for RING1B association with CGIs, RING1B ChIP-seq signal from the control and KDM2B KD cell lines was initially plotted over previously identified RING1B CGI associated target sites (Figure 6C). This revealed a specific reduction in RING1B signal at these sites following KDM2B knockdown in fitting with a role for KDM2B in RING1B targeting.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis in Figure 6C

claim: Depletion of KDM2B results in an even more dramatic effect on RING1B occupancy at novel low magnitude sites.
source: Interestingly, depletion of KDM2B resulted in an even more dramatic effect on RING1B occupancy at these novel low magnitude sites, suggesting that these RING1B binding events are more dependent on KDM2B.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 6D,F

claim: KDM2B plays a widespread role in targeting RING1B in vivo both at established polycomb-repressed CGI-associated genes and a novel class of lower magnitude RING1B occupied CGI sites.
source: Together these observations indicate that KDM2B plays a widespread role in targeting RING1B in vivo both at previously identified established polycomb-repressed CGI-associated genes and a novel class of lower magnitude RING1B occupied CGI sites.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-seq analysis of RING1B in KDM2B knockdown cells

claim: Depletion of KDM2B results in an approximately 40% global reduction of H2AK119ub1.
source: Interestingly, depletion of KDM2B results in an approximately 40% global reduction of this modification, indicating that KDM2B contributes significantly to H2AK119ub1 at the genome scale, most likely due to its widespread role in guiding RING1B occupancy.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot quantification in Figure 7A,B

claim: KDM2B knockdown does not cause global changes in levels of H3K27me3, H3K4me3 or H3K36me2.
source: This was not the result of more general changes in chromatin modification as other histone marks including H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 were largely unaffected (Figure 7C).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis in Figure 7C

claim: Reductions in H2AK119ub1 in KDM2B knockdown cells appear to be restricted to polycomb target CGIs that were up-regulated in the absence of KDM2B.
source: Interestingly reductions in H2AK119ub1 appeared to be restricted to the polycomb target CGIs that were up-regulated in the absence of KMD2B (Figure 7D).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP analysis in Figure 7D

claim: H2AK119ub1 reduction at individual genes correlates with a more subtle reduction in H3K27me3 but largely unchanged levels of H3K4me3.
source: This also correlated with a more subtle reduction in H3K27me3 but largely unchanged levels of H3K4me3 (Figure 7D).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP analysis in Figure 7D

claim: Some polycomb repressed sites rely more specifically on KDM2B mediated RING1B occupancy for normal H2AK119ub1 and polycomb mediated gene repression.
source: Together these observations suggest that some polycomb repressed sites rely more specifically on KDM2B mediated RING1B occupancy for normal H2AK119ub1 and polycomb mediated gene repression (Endoh et al., 2012).
evidence: Inferred from ChIP and gene expression data, supported by cited study

claim: KDM2B specifically recognizes non-methylated DNA in CGIs.
source: Here we demonstrate that KDM2B recognizes CGI elements via its ZF-CxxC domain and in contrast to its paralogue, KDM2A, is preferentially enriched at polycomb-repressed CGIs in mouse ESCs (Figure 2).
evidence: Demonstrated by EMSA and ChIP-seq data

claim: KDM2B recruits the polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1) to CGIs.
source: Here we discover that KDM2B (FBXL10) specifically recognizes non-methylated DNA in CGIs and recruits the polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1).
evidence: Demonstrated by protein complex purification, ChIP-seq, and functional studies

claim: KDM2B contributes to histone H2A lysine 119 ubiquitylation (H2AK119ub1) and gene repression.
source: This contributes to histone H2A lysine 119 ubiquitylation (H2AK119ub1) and gene repression.
evidence: Demonstrated by H2AK119ub1 ChIP and gene expression analysis

claim: CGIs are occupied by low levels of PRC1 throughout the genome.
source: Unexpectedly, we also find that CGIs are occupied by low levels of PRC1 throughout the genome, suggesting that the KDM2B-PRC1 complex may sample CGI-associated genes for susceptibility to polycomb-mediated silencing.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis revealing widespread low-level RING1B binding

claim: The KDM2B-PRC1 complex may sample CGI-associated genes for susceptibility to polycomb-mediated silencing.
source: Unexpectedly, we also find that CGIs are occupied by low levels of PRC1 throughout the genome, suggesting that the KDM2B-PRC1 complex may sample CGI-associated genes for susceptibility to polycomb-mediated silencing.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of widespread low-level RING1B binding data

claim: CGIs function as mammalian PREs.
source: These observations demonstrate an unexpected and direct link between recognition of CGIs by KDM2B and targeting of the polycomb repressive system. This provides the basis for a new model describing the functionality of CGIs as mammalian PREs.
evidence: Inferred from the mechanistic link between KDM2B, CGI recognition, and PRC1 targeting

claim: In mammals, the majority of CpG dinucleotides are methylated on the 5 position of cytosine.
source: In mammals, the majority of CpG dinucleotides are methylated on the 5 position of cytosine and this epigenetic modification can be stably transmitted across cell divisions (Klose and Bird, 2006).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited reference

claim: DNA methylation is thought to be a highly stable modification that helps maintain intergenic and heterochromatic regions in a transcriptionally inert chromatin state.
source: DNA methylation is thought to be a highly stable modification that helps maintain intergenic and heterochromatic regions in a transcriptionally inert chromatin state (Bird, 2002; Klose and Bird, 2006).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited references

claim: CGIs lack DNA methylation and are associated with roughly two-thirds of human gene promoters.
source: A major exception to this pervasive methylation is short contiguous regions of the genome, called CpG islands (CGIs), which lack DNA methylation and are associated with roughly two-thirds of human gene promoters (Illingworth and Bird, 2009).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited reference

claim: CGIs function to buffer gene regulatory elements from the repressive effects of surrounding DNA methylation.
source: It is thought that CGIs function to buffer gene regulatory elements from the repressive effects of surrounding DNA methylation and therefore play a central role in the regulatory capacity of the genome (Blackledge and Klose, 2011).
evidence: Established model supported by cited reference

claim: Non-methylated CpG dinucleotides found within CGIs act as a binding site for proteins that contain the ZF-CxxC DNA binding domain.
source: Although for the past two decades CGIs were considered to play a largely passive role in promoter and regulatory element function, we and others recently discovered that the non-methylated CpG dinucleotides found within CGIs act as a binding site for proteins that contain the ZF-CxxC DNA binding domain (Blackledge et al., 2010; Thomson et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by cited studies including authors' previous work

claim: CFP1 is a core component of the SET1 histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4) methyltransferase complex.
source: For example, the ZF-CxxC domain containing protein CFP1 is a core component of the SET1 histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4) methyltransferase complex (Lee and Skalnik, 2005) and targets this transcriptionally permissive modification to CGIs genome-wide.
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited reference

claim: KDM2A histone H3K36 demethylase enzyme contains a ZF-CxxC domain that targets the enzyme directly to CGIs where it removes histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36) dimethylation.
source: Similarly, the KDM2A histone H3K36 demethylase enzyme contains a ZF-CxxC domain that targets the enzyme directly to CGIs where it removes histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36) dimethylation (Blackledge et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by cited study from authors' previous work

claim: H3K36me1/me2 is found broadly across the genome in mammals.
source: In mammals H3K36me1/me2 is found broadly across the genome (Peters et al., 2003; Robin et al., 2007; Blackledge et al., 2010) and may be inhibitory to transcriptional initiation (Strahl et al., 2002; Carrozza et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: Targeting of chromatin modifications to CGI associated gene promoters generally occurs independently of the transcriptional state of the associated gene.
source: Importantly, the targeting of these modifications to CGI associated gene promoters generally occurs independently of the transcriptional state of the associated gene (Blackledge et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by cited study from authors' previous work

claim: PRC1 complexes have E3 ubiquitin ligase activity that mono-ubiquitylates H2A on position 119 (H2AK119ub1).
source: PRC1 complexes have E3 ubiquitin ligase activity that mono-ubiquitylates H2A on position 119 (H2AK119ub1) (Wang et al., 2004b; de Napoles et al., 2004) and PRC2 complexes have histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) methyltransferase activity (Cao et al., 2002; Czermin et al., 2002; Kuzmichev et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited references

claim: PRC2 complexes have histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) methyltransferase activity.
source: PRC1 complexes have E3 ubiquitin ligase activity that mono-ubiquitylates H2A on position 119 (H2AK119ub1) (Wang et al., 2004b; de Napoles et al., 2004) and PRC2 complexes have histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) methyltransferase activity (Cao et al., 2002; Czermin et al., 2002; Kuzmichev et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited references

claim: Polycomb mediated chromatin modifications are thought to generate a more compact and inhibitory chromatin environment, limiting transcription of associated genes.
source: In contrast to the permissive and accessible chromatin state found at most CGIs, polycomb mediated chromatin modifications are thought to generate a more compact and inhibitory chromatin environment, limiting transcription of associated genes (Shao et al., 1999; Lavigne et al., 2004; Francis et al., 2004; Eskeland et al., 2010).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited references

claim: In Drosophila, polycomb repressive complexes are targeted to polycomb response elements (PREs) through the action of transcription factors.
source: In Drosophila, which lack CGIs, polycomb repressive complexes are targeted to regions of the genome called polycomb response elements (PREs) through the action of transcription factors (reviewed in (Schuettengruber et al., 2007; Ringrose and Paro, 2007; Simon and Kingston, 2009)).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by cited reviews

claim: In mammals, PREs predominantly correspond to CGIs.
source: Interestingly, in mammals this situation is very different in that PREs predominantly correspond to CGIs (Ku et al., 2008; Woo et al., 2010) and there is mounting evidence that chromatin features specific to CGIs may play an important role in guiding PRC complexes to these particular regions of the genome (Mendenhall et al., 2010; Kanhere et al., 2010; Lynch et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited references

claim: Novel RING1B associated CGI genes are expressed at similar levels to non-RING1B associated CGI genes.
source: On average, novel RING1B associated CGI associated genes are expressed at similar levels to non-RING1B associated CGI genes (median signal of 10.47 vs 10.24).
evidence: Demonstrated by microarray analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3

claim: Established RING1B associated CGIs are on average expressed at lower levels than novel RING1B CGIs.
source: In contrast, established RING1B associated CGIs are on average expressed at lower levels (median signal of 8.47).
evidence: Demonstrated by microarray analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3

claim: PRC1 is thought to be mechanistically recruited in a hierarchical manner through chromo-domain mediated recognition of H3K27 methylation at pre-existing PRC2 modified sites.
source: In most species PRC1 is thought to be mechanistically recruited in a hierarchical manner through chromo-domain mediated recognition of H3K27 methylation at pre-existing PRC2 modified sites (Cao et al., 2002; Min et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2004b).
evidence: Established model supported by cited references

claim: H3K27 independent PRC1 targeting mechanisms are sufficient to maintain H2AK119ub1 and repression at many PRC1 bound targets.
source: However, the singularity of the hierarchal recruitment mechanism has recently been challenged by a series of elegant experiments in mammals demonstrating that although genetic perturbation of the PRC2 complexes reduces PRC1 localization to polycomb repressed CGIs (Tavares et al., 2012), H3K27 independent PRC1 targeting mechanisms are sufficient to maintain H2AK119ub1 and repression at many PRC1 bound targets (Schoeftner et al., 2006; Pasini et al., 2007; Leeb et al., 2010; Tavares et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple cited studies

claim: The KDM2B-PRC1 complex provides an alternative mechanism for PRC1 recognition of polycomb repressed CGIs in mammals.
source: Based on our observations that KDM2B is important for RING1B binding to CGI elements, the KDM2B-PRC1 complex provides an alternative mechanism for PRC1 recognition of polycomb repressed CGIs in mammals.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing KDM2B-dependent RING1B targeting

claim: KDM2B depletion in embryonic stem cells results in up-regulation of only a subset of PRC1 target genes.
source: This is supported by the observation that KDM2B depletion in embryonic stem cells results in up-regulation of only a subset of PRC1 target genes.
evidence: Demonstrated by gene expression analysis

claim: Polycomb repression may rely on the combined activity of hierarchical recruitment and alternative direct targeting mechanisms as an important stability component for maintenance of the silenced state.
source: Therefore, one can envision that polycomb repression, which must be maintained over cell divisions and developmental time scales, may rely on the combined activity of these separate pathways as an important stability component for maintenance of the silenced state.
evidence: Speculative model based on experimental observations
